parts.title: The first week at a new job
parts.instructions: Read the story and choose the best answer.
parts.passage:
I started my first job at a small travel company in June. I expected to spend most of the day answering the phone, but my manager, Jo, had other plans. On my first morning she showed me how to update the company’s website. I was nervous because I had only made a school page before.

Jo didn’t give me a long list of instructions. Instead, she asked me to try one small change and then show it to her. When I made a mistake, she explained what had happened and let me correct it. By Friday, I had added information about three new walking tours.

The best surprise was meeting the guides. They came to the office to tell us about the places they visited with customers. I began to understand why people enjoyed working there. The job is busy, and I still have a lot to learn, but I feel comfortable asking questions now.

questions.prompt: What did the writer expect to do at work?
options: Take customers out on the walking tours
Answer the phone most of the time
questions.explanation: She says she expected to spend most of the day answering the phone.

questions.prompt: Why was the writer nervous?
options: They did not know any of the guides well
They had little experience making websites
The company website was not working
Jo expected too much from them
questions.explanation: She was nervous because she had only made a school page before, so she had little experience.

questions.prompt: How did Jo help the writer learn?
options: She sent them on a training course
She gave them a long manual
She asked them to try small tasks
She completed the work for them
questions.explanation: Jo asked her to try one small change and then show it to her.

questions.prompt: What did the writer do by Friday?
options: Added three tours to the website
Changed the name of the company
Met all of the people who buy tours
Took a group of visitors around
questions.explanation: By Friday she had added information about three new walking tours to the website.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel now?
options: Worried about the other new colleagues
More confident about asking for help
questions.explanation: She says she feels comfortable asking questions now, so she is more confident about asking for help.

parts.title: The school radio station
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Our school started a radio station last year. At first, only a few students were interested. [1] Then our English teacher suggested making a weekly programme about music and school news.

We had to learn how to use the recording equipment. [2] After a few attempts, we could edit the interviews ourselves.

The first programme was only ten minutes long. [3] Students began sending in questions and asking to hear their favourite songs.

Now the radio team meets every Wednesday lunchtime. [4] We also record interviews with teachers and visitors.

I have learned to plan ahead and speak clearly. [5] Next term, we hope to broadcast a live quiz.
sentences: Radio stations usually need a licence from the government.
Nearly everyone in school listened to it.
Our school has about eight hundred students.
We play it during lunch on Fridays.
It has also made me much less shy in front of other people.
Most of us had never used a microphone before.
Many people thought it would be difficult to manage.
The music was too loud for the classroom.

gaps.explanation: “Many people thought it would be difficult to manage” explains why few students were interested at first, and “Then” introduces the teacher’s idea.
“Most of us had never used a microphone before” explains why they had to learn the equipment, and “After a few attempts” follows.
“Nearly everyone in school listened to it” fits after the short first programme and leads to students sending questions.
“We play it during lunch on Fridays” follows the team’s Wednesday meeting; “it” is the programme. “We also record” adds more.
“It has also made me much less shy” adds to what the writer has learned, before the plan for next term.

parts.title: A useful placement
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Last summer I did a work [1] at a local hotel. I wanted to [2] experience before starting college. The manager asked me to [3] guests when they arrived and show them to their rooms. At first I was shy, but I soon got [4] to speaking to new people. My colleagues were kind and gave me helpful [5]. I would [6] the placement to anyone interested in tourism.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: A work placement is a period of work experience; the other nouns do not fit “do a work ...”.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You gain experience; you do not win, earn or buy it in this sense.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: You welcome guests when they arrive and show them to their rooms.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: “Get used to” + -ing means become familiar with.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: Colleagues give helpful advice; news, permission and luck do not fit “gave me helpful ...”.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: You recommend something to someone; the other verbs do not fit “the placement to anyone”.

parts.title: A message about a course
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Marta,
I’ve signed up [1] an evening photography course. It starts next week and lasts [2] six weeks. We’ll meet in the art room, [3] is on the second floor. I’m excited [4] I’ve wanted to learn how to use my camera properly. You should come [5] me if you’re free. The teacher says we can bring photos [6] we have taken ourselves.
See you,
Lucy

gaps.explanation: We sign up for a course.
A course lasts for six weeks.
The relative pronoun “which” refers to the art room and starts a non-defining clause.
“Because” gives the reason she is excited: she has wanted to learn.
We say “come with me” when we invite someone to join us.
“Photos that we have taken ourselves” defines which photos.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: sophie

turns.speaker: sophie

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: So where do they want us?

turns.speaker: sophie
turns.text: The room at the end of the corridor, next to the lift. Number eight.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Oh, good. It has the big window. What time again?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Will do. See you there.

turns.speaker: lena

turns.speaker: hugo

turns.speaker: chris
turns.text: Fatima, I thought you’d be at your desk by now. Is the train late again?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: Worse. There’s a strike, and nothing is running until tomorrow. I did think about driving, but the car park near the office is full.

turns.speaker: chris

turns.speaker: fatima

turns.speaker: isla
turns.text: Did you look at the jobs, Omari?

turns.speaker: omari
turns.text: Yes. The museum job sounds the most interesting, honestly. I’d love it.

turns.speaker: isla

turns.speaker: omari

turns.speaker: omari

question.explanation: Omari nearly applied for the interesting museum job, but he chooses the library advert because it saves him an hour a day and is close to where he lives.

turns.text: Jonas, that was a good presentation. I could hear every word, so you don’t have to speak more loudly.

turns.speaker: jonas
turns.text: Thanks. I practised in the garden so I wouldn’t be too quiet.

turns.speaker: bea
turns.text: It worked. Your notes were useful, too. Some students write whole paragraphs, but yours were short.

turns.speaker: jonas
turns.text: I used cards this time. Is there anything I should change?

turns.speaker: bea
turns.text: Just one thing. You kept staring at the floor, so the audience didn’t feel you were talking to them. Try looking up for a few seconds after each point.

turns.speaker: jonas

question.explanation: Ms Bea praises his voice and short notes; her advice is to look up at the people in the room after each point.

turns.speaker: vikram
turns.text: Rita, could you help me with the moving boxes this week?

turns.speaker: rita

turns.speaker: vikram

turns.speaker: rita

turns.speaker: rita

turns.speaker: vikram

turns.speaker: raj

turns.speaker: raj

turns.speaker: raj
turns.text: That’s a long wait.

turns.speaker: daisy

question.explanation: The course was due to begin tomorrow, but the teacher is injured, so the centre moved it to the start of next month.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea

turns.speaker: pavel

turns.speaker: anita

turns.speaker: holt

turns.speaker: anita

turns.speaker: dylan
turns.text: Have you finished the book for class?

turns.speaker: zara
turns.text: Almost. The first chapters were hard. I had to use the dictionary a lot.

turns.speaker: dylan
turns.text: Me too. But after chapter five I couldn’t stop reading.

turns.speaker: zara

It is hard to put down

turns.speaker: ross
turns.text: So, Carla, what would you like to work on today?

turns.speaker: carla

turns.speaker: ross

turns.speaker: carla

turns.speaker: nadia

parts.title: A talk about a training course
parts.instructions: Listen and complete the notes. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time in each gap.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Welcome to the training centre. I’m Mark, and I’ll explain how the course works. Our first class is on Monday at six o’clock. Some of you were told Tuesday in the email, but that was a mistake, so please remember Monday. Please come to the main hall, where you’ll receive your books. Don’t go to the library, because it’s closed for repairs this month. The hall is the large room on the ground floor, just behind the reception desk. You should bring a notebook and a pen. A pencil isn’t necessary, because we’ll mainly write short answers and notes about our discussions. Each lesson lasts two hours, and we take a short break at seven thirty. At eight o’clock, we start the second half, which is usually the practical part. The lesson ends at nine. If you need something to eat, there is a café on the ground floor next to the hall. There are also vending machines on the first floor, but they sometimes run out of drinks. The café closes early, so bring a snack if you need one. Now, some information about the length of the course. The full programme lasts eight weeks. A longer programme, which is twelve weeks, is for the advanced group, and you’ll hear about that later. At the end of the eighth week, there is a short test, and then you receive a certificate. If you miss a class, please tell your teacher in advance. Finally, our phone number is on the back of your book, and the office is open every morning. Thank you for listening, and I hope you enjoy the course.

gaps.explanation: Mark says Tuesday in the email was a mistake, so the first class is on Monday.

gaps.prompt: Students collect their books in the large ___ behind reception
gaps.explanation: He says not to go to the library, which is closed; they receive the books in the main hall.
Mark says to bring a notebook and a pen; a pencil is not necessary.

gaps.prompt: The short break is at ___ in the evening
gaps.explanation: The break is at seven thirty, before the second half starts at eight.

gaps.prompt: The café is on the ___ floor
gaps.explanation: He says the vending machines are on the first floor, but the café is on the ground floor next to the hall.
The full programme lasts eight weeks; twelve weeks is only for the advanced group.

parts.title: An interview with a teacher
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tom, you’ve been a teacher for fifteen years. Why did you become one?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: It wasn’t because of the holidays, although everybody says that. And my family didn’t push me, they wanted me to be an accountant. At school I had a history teacher who made the past feel alive. I remember walking out of her classroom and wanting to give other students the same feeling.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your first year like?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: Busy! Finding a classroom wasn’t the problem, they gave me a nice one on the second floor. And I knew my history, I’d studied it for years. What took all my evenings was preparing the lessons. I spent hours making worksheets, and I was exhausted. Luckily my colleagues helped me, and I learned to plan more carefully.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you enjoy most about teaching now?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: I like writing the end-of-year reports less than people think, and organising trips is more stress than fun. What I enjoy is the moment when a student understands something that seemed impossible ten minutes before. You can see it in their faces. Every class is different, so the work never feels boring.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What is the most challenging part?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: It’s not choosing textbooks, the school does that, and I’m rarely late for a lesson. The real challenge is keeping everyone involved. Some students are very confident and answer every question, while others need more time and stay quiet. If I’m not careful, the loud ones take over and the others quietly switch off and stop listening completely.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you deal with that?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: I never give extra homework to the quiet ones, that would only make them hate the subject. And I can’t split a class of thirty into small groups, there isn’t the space. So I change the activities. We might have a debate, then a game, then a writing task, so that everybody can find something that suits them.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give a new teacher?

turns.speaker: tom
turns.text: Follow your plan at the start, it gives you confidence. But listen to your students, because they can tell you what is working. And don’t be afraid to change a lesson in the middle if the class needs something different. Some of my best lessons began as a mistake, and it took me years to be comfortable with that idea.

questions.prompt: Why did Tom decide to teach?
questions.explanation: Tom says it was not for the holidays or for his family; a history teacher made the past feel alive and he wanted to give students the same feeling.

questions.prompt: What did Tom find difficult in his first year?
questions.explanation: Finding a classroom was easy and he knew history; what took his evenings was preparing lessons.

questions.prompt: What does Tom enjoy most?
questions.explanation: Tom says he likes reports and trips less than people think; he enjoys the moment when a student understands something difficult.

questions.prompt: What is his biggest challenge?
options: Choosing a good textbook for each class
Starting every lesson exactly on time
questions.explanation: Textbooks are chosen by the school and he is rarely late; the real challenge is keeping everyone involved.

questions.prompt: How does Tom help different students?

parts.title: Getting to know you
